text: C4 holds up a picture frame with ‘Scene 5’ on the back
speaker: C4

text: Scene 5
speaker: C4

text: C4 turns the frame round to reveal a picture of Sibyl’s Kitchen
speaker: C4

text: Sibyl Vane
speaker: C1/4

text: The Vane’s dingy sitting-room contained one arm-chair. Mrs Vane…
speaker: C4

text: a faded, tired-looking woman,
speaker: Mrs V C2

text: was sitting in it, with her back turned to the shrill intrusive light
speaker: C5

text: Mother, I am so happy and you must be happy, too!
speaker: Sibyl

text: Happy! I am only happy, Sibyl, when I see you act.  You must not think of anything but your acting.  Mr. Isaacs has been very good to us, and we owe him money.
speaker: Mrs.V

text: Money, Mother? What does money matter?  Love is more than money.
speaker: Sibyl

text: Mr. Isaacs has advanced us fifty pounds to pay off our debts and to get a proper outfit for James.
speaker: Mrs V

text: He is not a gentleman, Mother, and I hate the way he talks to me.
speaker: Sibyl

text: I don't know how we could manage without him.
speaker: Mrs V

text: We don't want him any more, Mother.  Prince Charming is all that matters now. I love him.
speaker: Sibyl

text: My child, you are far too young to think of falling in love.  What do you know of this young man?  You don't even know his name.  The whole thing is most inconvenient, and really, when James is going away to Australia, and I have so much to think of, I must say that you should have shown more consideration. Although, if he is rich ...
speaker: Mrs V

text: Ah!  Mother, Mother, let me be happy!
speaker: Sibyl

text: Sibyl kisses her mother
speaker: Stage

text: (enters) You might keep some of your kisses for me, Sibyl, I think.
speaker: James

text: But you don't like being kissed, Jim.You are a dreadful old bear. (she hugs him)
speaker: Sibyl

text: I want you to come out with me for a walk, Sibyl. Put your best bonnet on.(she exits)
speaker: James

text: When you have made your fortune in Australia, you must come back and assert yourself in London.
speaker: Mrs V

text: I should like to make some money to take you and Sibyl off the stage.  I hate it.
speaker: James

text: Nonsense.  She has many admirers.
speaker: Mrs V

text: Mother, you must watch over Sibyl. Don't let her come to any harm.I hear a gentleman comes every night to the theatre and goes behind to talk to her. What about that?
speaker: James

text: You are speaking about things you don't understand, James.  I myself used to receive many bouquets at one time.  I do not know at present whether Sybil’s attachment is serious or not.  The young man in question is a perfect gentleman.  He is always most polite to me. Besides, he has the appearance of being rich, and the flowers he sends are lovely.
speaker: Mrs V

text: You don't know his name, though.
speaker: James

text: No, He has not yet revealed his real name.  I think it is quite romantic of him.  He is probably a member of the aristocracy. To Sibyl he is Prince Charming.
speaker: Mrs V

text: Believe me that if this man wrongs my sister, I will find out who he is, track him down, and kill him like a dog. I swear it.
speaker: James

text: (Sibyl enters)
speaker: Stage

text: How serious you both are. What is the matter?
speaker: Sibyl

text: Nothing I suppose one must be serious sometimes.
speaker: James

text: (they start walking)
speaker: Stage

text: (removes chair) They went out into the flickering, wind-blown sunlight and strolled down the dreary Euston Road. (holds Euston Road Sign)
speaker: C4

text: Chorus become passersby
speaker: Stage

text: You are not listening to a word I am saying. Do say something.
speaker: Sibyl

text: You have a new friend, I hear.  Who is he?  Why have you not told me about him?  He means you no good.
speaker: James

text: You must not say anything against him.  I love him.
speaker: Sibyl

text: Why, you don't even know his name.  Who is he?
speaker: James

text: He is called Prince Charming. Oh, Jim! If you only saw him, you would think him the most wonderful person in the world.  Everybody likes him, and I ... love him. I wish you could come to the theatre to-night. He is going to be there, and I am to play Juliet.
speaker: Sibyl

text: He is a gentleman. He wants to enslave you. I want you to beware of him. As sure as there is a God in heaven, if he ever does you any wrong, I shall kill him.
speaker: James

text: You are foolish, Jim, utterly foolish. You don't know what you are talking about. Love makes people good, and what you said was wicked.
speaker: Sibyl

text: Mother is no help to you.  She doesn't understand how to look after you.
speaker: James

text: Oh, don't be so serious, Jim. I know you would never harm anyone I love, would you?
speaker: Sibyl

text: Not as long as you love him, I suppose.
speaker: James

text: I shall love him forever!
speaker: Sibyl

text: And he?
speaker: James

text: Forever, too!
speaker: Sibyl

text: He had better.
speaker: James
